narrative.title: Sequencing the One-Way Pipeline Costs
narrative.scenario: A build pipeline's stages run one-way with per-stage tolls, and DevOps wants the cheapest toll total from stage 0 to every stage. Because no stage ever loops back, one pass in dependency order suffices: settle a stage's cheapest toll first, then relax its outgoing one-way edges — each edge relaxes once, forever.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer N (vertices 0..N-1), the edge count M, and an edge list edges where [u, v, w] is a one-way edge u -> v with cost w.
narrative.outputFormat: Return an array where entry i is the minimum cost from vertex 0 to i, or -1 if unreachable.

testCases.explanation: Stage 3 is cheapest via 0->2 (1) then 2->3 (1): total 2.
Vertex 2 has no incoming edges, so it stays unreachable.

hintLevels: Level 1: In a one-way graph there is a safe order to settle costs — dependencies first.
Level 2: Topologically sort, initialize source to 0 and the rest to infinity, then relax each edge exactly once.
Level 3: Any vertex still at infinity after the sweep has no incoming path — flip it to -1.
